full_judgment: 3. That, the defendant Nos. 1 to 4, 16 and 17 appeared in the suit and submitted written statement denying all the plaint allegations and contending inter alia that 66.16 (30.92 khas and 35.25 tenanted) acres of land recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 232, which is the suit holding originally belonged to Umacharan and 8 others. Those tenants and/or their successors and assignee defaulted in paying rent for which the entire holding was sold in auction on 27.09.1954 vide certificate case No. 252/1953-54. The defendant Nos. 1 to 4 purchased the auction (defendant Nos. 1 to 3 to the extent of 8 annas jointly and defendant No.4 to the extent of rest 8 annas) and got delivery of possession through the process of law on 03.10.54. At the time of such auction purchase 43.53 acres of land was khas land of the holding; the defendant No.4 filed title suit No.117/1957 in the court sub-ordinate Judge, Khulna against the defendant No.1 to 3 for partition of her 1/2 (half) share out of Khas 43.53 acres of land of the holding and got decree on 12.09.1957 for the same. Since then she had been possessing her share separately while the defendant nos. 1 to 3 had been possessing their shares jointly. One Kamala Bala Dashi and others instituted Title Suit No. 94 of 1961 in the 1st Court of Munsiff, Khulna for setting aside the aforesaid auction sale on the plea of purchase from one of the decedents of original tenant and suppressing summons thereof obtained fraudulent decree dated 18.4.1964 beyond the knowledge of the auction purchasers. That, Samir Chardra Singha one of the full brothers of the plaintiffs purchased 1.00 acre of land by successive transfer from the defendant No.4, which was sold to the defendant No. 16 by Registered sale deed dated 25.8.1987; Satish Chandra Singha purchased 1.66 acres of land from the defendant No.4 by Registered sale deed dated 03.12.1957 and another 1.66 acres of land from the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by Registered sale deed dated 08.03.1979 and by such purchase, father of the plaintiffs being in possession of 3.32 acres of land died leaving behind the plaintiffs and two other sons named Tapan and Samir. The plaintiffs and their brothers Tapan and Samir being is possession of the said 3.32 acres of land sold 1.66 acres of land jointly to Puspa Rani by Registered Sale Deed dated 04.07.1984 and delivered possession. Subsequently, the plaintiffs nos. 1, 2, 3, 5 and their full brothers Tapan and Samir jointly sold 1.66 acres of land to the defendant No. 17 and one Ranjit Kumar by Registered sale deed dated 30.07.1988. The claim of the plaintiffs as made out in the plaint has been waived and they have been estopped by executing and Registering sale deed dated 04.07.1984 and 30.7.1988 knowing of the fraudulent decree passed in title suit No. 94 of 1961, within time the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 instituted Title no. 210 of 1969 in the 1st Court of Munsiff, Khulna. The plaintiffs as defendant Nos. 30 to 34 of that suit on receipt of summons appeared in that suit but ultimately finding no defence, refrained from contesting the suit like other defendants. Ultimately Title Suit No 210 of 1969 was decreed ex-parte on 15.02.1972. One Sachindra Nath Das and others filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 being Miscellaneous Case No.389 of 1972 for setting aside the decree dated 15.02.1972 passed in title suit no. 210 of 1969 which was ultimately dismissed on compromise. Again one Krishna Pada and others filed Miscellaneous Case No. 415 of 1974 under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for setting aside the decree dated 15.02.1972 passed in Title Suit No. 210 of 1969; which was also dismissed on compromise.
